opening.headline: The problem of the assistant referring to old prices even though the price list has been revised is solved by uploading or linking the data according to the update frequency.
body: The price list file uploaded in March remains in the project, and the new price list revised in April is separate. The assistant confidently provides the March price, not the new price. The sales team thinks the assistant is wrong, but the assistant just answered based on the data she had.

In this lesson, we start from the fact that the uploaded file is a copy of the time it was uploaded. Divide the uploaded and linked materials according to the frequency with which the materials change, and learn the risks of placing the same material in two places and the principles of keeping the source as one. At the end, we explain with examples how to handle company regulations, inventory status, and price lists.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the difference between fixed and variable data
Storage methods can be classified based on the frequency of data update.

screens.title: I posted a price list, but even after revision, it says the old price.
screens.lead: First, let's look at what happens when the price lists before and after revision are left together. Also consider whose fault it is.

visual.alt: Two price lists before and after revision on the left, and a response stating the old price on the right.
labels: How much does a ballpoint pen cost?

paragraphs: The price list file posted in March remains in the project. In April the prices were revised and a new price list was released, and someone uploaded the file but did not delete the old file.
When sales ask for prices, the assistant confidently tells them the March prices, not the new prices. The sales team thinks the assistant is wrong, but the assistant answers based on the data he has.
The question for this class is this. How should we handle changing data and non-changing data differently?

screens.outro: First, let's think about your data management experience.

screens.title: How do you manage frequently updated materials?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think first before clicking.

items.prompt: Which of the materials I write changes more than once a month?
items.answer: Common examples include price lists, inventory status, contact information, and ongoing project status. These materials start to age the moment you put them on the Assistant. This class focuses on how to work with this material.

items.prompt: Who is responsible for deleting old files after revisions?
items.answer: If there is no designated person in charge, the person who uploaded the new file is expected to have deleted the old file, and the administrator expects the person who posted it to have deleted it. As a result, old files remain. Establishing replacement responsibilities and procedures takes precedence over technology.

items.prompt: Can we treat data that changes once a year and data that changes every day in the same way?
items.answer: It must not be handled. You can upload data that changes once a year and replace it only when it is revised, but data that changes every day becomes outdated the moment you upload it. Frequency of renewal determines storage method.

screens.outro: Now that we've summarized our experience, let's start by looking at the properties of the uploaded file.

screens.title: Static knowledge: The file you upload is a copy of the moment it was uploaded.
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow how your uploaded copy remains while the original is being revised.

visual.alt: The original and the uploaded copy become misaligned over time.

steps.title: What is static knowledge?
steps.body: Static knowledge is knowledge that is fixed to the content at the time of upload, such as an uploaded file. The moment you upload a file, a copy of its contents will be placed next to your Assistant. This copy is not connected to the original.

steps.title: March: Original and copy are the same
steps.body: I posted the original price list in March. At this point, the content of the original and uploaded copy is the same, so the price quoted by the assistant is correct. Because it seems harmless, it's easy to forget that these files will become outdated later.

steps.title: April: Only the original changes
steps.body: The original price was revised in April. However, the uploaded copy did not change. The assistant cannot tell that the original has been changed and answers based on the copy it has, so discrepancies begin.

steps.title: As time goes by, the discrepancy increases.
steps.body: As revisions continue, the difference between the original and the copy increases. At this point, the Assistant will continue to speak the old values ​​unless you replace the copy. According to the ChatGPT project instructions, uploaded files can be previewed, downloaded, and deleted from the source list. To replace it, you need to upload the new file and delete the old file. Also keep in mind that if you delete a file from a shared project, it's gone for everyone.

steps.title: Static knowledge is suitable data
steps.body: Therefore, static knowledge is suitable for data that does not change. Like company regulations, glossaries, and stable parts of product manuals, these are materials that are used for a long time once uploaded. If you upload frequently changing materials as static knowledge, outdated copies will accumulate.

screens.outro: Since the speed of change is different for each data, let's now look at the standard for determining the method based on the update frequency.

screens.title: Update frequency: The method is determined by how often things change.
screens.lead: Move the slider to change the data change cycle in the order of year, month, week, and day. You can see that the appropriate storage method and risk vary depending on the cycle.

visual.alt: A tabular diagram showing the appropriate storage method depending on the frequency of data update.

stops.body: Uploading data that changes about once a year, such as company regulations, is not burdensome. Just put it up and replace it once when revising. The risk is forgetting to revise, so put the revision date in the file name and assign a person responsible for revision. You can easily tell if the material is out of date by having your assistant mention the revision date along with the answer.

Materials that change about once a month, such as price lists, require a responsible department and procedure to replace them each time they are revised. Unless you have a set procedure for uploading new files and deleting old files on the same day, both versions will remain together. If replacement becomes cumbersome or is missed frequently, consider moving to a connected method.

It is difficult to keep up with uploads of data that changes on a weekly basis. The replacement cycle is short, so the burden on the person in charge is high, and if one is missed, old data is used for a week. For these materials, a linking method that allows the assistant to read directly from where the original is located is appropriate.

It is virtually impossible to manage data that changes daily, such as inventory status, by uploading it. You will need to connect to your inventory system or Drive file. ChatGPT lets you attach Google Drive files, folders, or Slack channel links as project sources, keeping your work in the latest context. However, the Drive app added to the project is not synchronized in advance, but is instructed to search and import it.

screens.outro: Now that we know the criteria for frequency, let's look at the risks of having the same data in two places and the principle of maintaining one source.

screens.title: Risks of double storage of data and maintaining a single source
screens.lead: Switch between uploading a copy and linking to the source and compare how the two methods react when the original is revised.

visual.alt: A drawing that juxtaposes a structure that contains the same data in two places and a structure that points to only one place.

states.label: Upload a copy
states.body: Dual archiving is the state of keeping the same material in the original and an uploaded copy, or in two copies. If you edit the original and don't replace the copy, the content in the two places will be different. If only one of the two is corrected, the assistant will mix up the old and the new, or sometimes use the other as the basis, resulting in inconsistent answers. Because people work with the original and assistants work with the copy, they sometimes end up giving different values. Dual storage builds up out of sight, so unless you intentionally reduce it, it will continue to grow.

states.label: Source Link
states.body: Maintaining one source is the principle of choosing one source of truth and having the assistant read from that source. When the original is revised, the assistant also reads the same original, reducing discrepancies. The Claude connector retrieves data from the services it connects to and respects each user's permissions. Files that are not accessible to users cannot be viewed by the connector. Drive links attached to ChatGPT projects are also introduced as a way to use the latest context in which the work lives. When connecting, you must also check who is reading and with what permissions.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the principles, let us explain how to deal with company regulations and inventory status.

screens.title: Explanation: How company regulations and inventory status are handled
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow the instructor as he takes turns processing company regulations and inventory status. Notice why the two materials are treated differently.

steps.title: Check out both sources
steps.body: Company regulations are revised once a year, and inventory status changes daily. Both are materials that the assistant uses when giving answers, but the speed at which they change is completely different. If treated in the same way, one side will inevitably become a problem.

steps.title: Sagyu: Upload as a knowledge file
steps.body: Since company regulations are revised once a year, they are uploaded as a knowledge file. Add the revision date to the file name to identify which version it is. For example, if you write it as Company Regulations_2026 Revision, it is easy to include the revision date in the instructions or answer.

steps.title: Company regulations: Decide on a replacement person
steps.body: When company regulations are revised, a person is appointed to delete old files and upload new files. Without responsibilities and procedures, both versions remain together. It is safest to have one person handle uploading and deleting on the same day.

steps.title: Inventory status: Connect without uploading
steps.body: Inventory status changes daily, so it is not uploaded to a file. Connect to your inventory system or Drive files and have your assistant read the original every time you ask a question. This way you don't end up guiding yesterday's inventory into today's inventory.

steps.title: Inventory Status: Determine the Method with Guidelines
steps.body: In the instructions, write a sentence saying that inventory questions should be answered by looking up linked inventory data, and if you don't know, say you don't have it. It is a device that prevents you from making up an answer when you cannot look it up.

steps.title: organizing
steps.body: In both cases, they had a single source and did not create dual archives. The source of company regulations is the uploaded file, and the source of inventory status is the linked original. Although the methods differed depending on the frequency of updates, the principle of one source was the same.

screens.outro: Next, let's look at the inspection procedure to prevent discrepancies in the price list example.

screens.title: Commentary: Inspection to prevent discrepancies after price list revision
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow how the price of your response changes as the revision process is applied one by one.

steps.title: 1. Raise a new price list
steps.body: Upload a new, revised price list file. At this stage the old files may still be there so the response may still be at the old price. Make it clear which files are new by including the revision date in the file name.

steps.title: 2. Delete old price tags on the same day
steps.body: Old price lists are deleted the same day. If it is a shared project, file deletion affects all members. If you notify members before deletion, they can store the necessary data separately. If the old file disappears, there will be no basis for the old price in the response.

steps.title: 3. Put pricing rules in your guidelines
steps.body: In the guidelines, there is a rule that the price only uses the value in the file, along with the revision date of the file name. If the revision date is included, users can immediately see if the material is out of date and avoid making up prices that are not in the file.

steps.title: 4. Check immediately after revision
steps.body: Immediately after the revision, ask two or three pricing questions to see if the new price comes up. The replacement is successful when the new price is displayed along with the revision date. If you see an old price, look to see if the old file is still there somewhere.

steps.title: 5. If revisions are frequent, change to connection.
steps.body: If this procedure is burdensome due to frequent revisions, replace the copy by linking the original price list. The upload and erase procedure itself disappears, and the assistant always reads the original value. However, keep in mind that connecting requires verification of access rights.

screens.outro: Now that we have checked the inspection procedures, let us summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaways
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class. As you read, try to answer the initial question: How do we treat changing and non-changing data differently?

paragraphs: The first question was how to handle changing and non-changing data differently. The uploaded file is a copy at the time of upload, so it will be out of sync if the original is changed. So, upload materials that are updated less frequently, but set a revision date and a person in charge of replacement. Do not upload materials that change frequently, but link to the original.

When choosing a connection, also look at access rights. The Claude connector follows the user permissions of the connected service, and the Drive app of the ChatGPT project searches and imports it without synchronizing it in advance. Since operations differ for each product, read and confirm the instructions.

Either way, the principle is to keep the source as one rather than placing the same material in two places. After revisions, we check to see if new values ​​result from representative questions, such as the price question.

Think back to the price tag in the first scene. Although the assistant thought he was wrong, he actually gave the correct answer based on an old copy. The problem was not with the model, but with how the data was managed. Remembering this distinction will help you avoid making mistakes where the cause of an incorrect answer is only found in the model.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Do not upload any material that changes, but link to it. If you need to upload it, put the revision date in the file name and specify the person in charge of replacing it and the date.

glossary.def: Like an uploaded file, it is fixed knowledge with the content at the time of upload.
This is a cycle in which data changes. It becomes the standard for deciding whether to upload or connect.

glossary.term: Risks of double storage of data
glossary.def: The problem is that the same data exists in two places, mixing old and new.
The principle is to set the source of data in one place and have the assistant read it from there.

misconceptions.myth: When you upload a new file, the old file is automatically replaced.
misconceptions.fact: If you don't delete old files, they will remain together and their contents will get mixed up. When you upload a new file, you must delete the old file on the same day.
Since frequently changing data needs to be replaced each time it is uploaded, linking it reduces the operational burden.

misconceptions.myth: When you attach a Drive link, it is always reflected in real time.
misconceptions.fact: Each product has a different synchronization method. The ChatGPT project's Drive app is guided by searching and importing without synchronizing in advance.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Do not upload any material that changes, but link to it.
The uploaded file is a copy of the time it was uploaded, so if the original is changed, it will be out of sync.
Update frequency determines upload and connection.
Keep the source code together rather than having the same material in two places.

checks.q: The price list was revised after being uploaded, but the assistant still says the old price. What is the best explanation?
options: This is a model error where the assistant ignores instructions.
This is because the uploaded file is a copy of the time it was uploaded, so it remains the same even if the original is changed.
This is because if you put the revision date in the file name, the old price will always appear.
This is because data connected through a connector is not updated once it is read.
checks.explain: Static knowledge is fixed to the content at the moment it is uploaded. If the original changes, you must either replace the copy or connect the original.

wrong.0: This is not a model error, but a discrepancy that occurs because the data is old.
wrong.2: Inserting the revision date into the file name actually helps distinguish which version it is.
wrong.3: The advantage of the connection method is that it follows the latest status because it reads the original.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: Match the update nature of your materials with the right management practices
left: Company regulations revised once a year
right: Set a replacement procedure for the person in charge and change the file every time it is revised.
Put the revision date in the file name and replace it only when revised.
Connect to inventory system or Drive file without uploading
checks.explain: Data that is rarely updated requires a small upload burden, data that changes daily needs to be properly connected, and data that changes on a monthly basis requires replacement staff and procedures.
